title: Processors: protect, clean, sample
summary: memory_limiter, batching in the exporter (the batch processor is on its way out), redaction with attributes, OTTL with transform and filter, and tail sampling policies.

steps.title: Protect the Collector, batch at the exporter
body: limit_mib: 400           # hard limit: refuse data (receivers return errors, SDKs retry)
spike_limit_mib: 80      # soft limit = limit - spike: start refusing early
sending_queue:           # queue + retries + batching, per exporter
- **memory_limiter** turns "OOM-killed and lost everything in flight" into "pushing back for a while". Also set `GOMEMLIMIT` to about
80% of the container limit so Go's garbage collector works with it.
- **Batching** used to be the `batch` processor. It is being deprecated in favour of exporter batching (`sending_queue.batch`), which
batches after the queue, per exporter; the replacement processor for the rare cases that need it is `queue_batch`. You will see
`batch` in almost every config written before 2027: it still works, and the release notes warn before it goes.
- `sending_queue` keeps data in memory while a backend is down (or on disk with the `file_storage` extension, to survive restarts).

steps.prompt: The backend is down for 10 minutes. The Collector has `memory_limiter` and an in-memory `sending_queue` of 1 000 batches. What happens?
options: The queue fills, then new data is dropped (counted in otelcol_exporter_enqueue_failed_*); memory_limiter keeps the Collector alive; when the backend returns the queue drains
The Collector buffers everything until the backend returns, however long it takes
The Collector crashes and restarts until the backend returns
SDKs keep the data until the Collector accepts it again
steps.explain: Every buffer is bounded. Size the queue for the outage you want to survive (throughput × time), use file_storage if a restart must not lose it, and alert on the enqueue_failed and send_failed metrics.

steps.prompt: Match the processor to the job.
pairs: Refuse data before the Collector runs out of memory
Keep every trace that had an error
Add pod and namespace names from the Kubernetes API

steps.title: Redact, rewrite, drop
body: attributes/redact:              # per-key actions on span, log and data point attributes
- { key: user.email, action: hash }        # SHA-256 hex of the value
- { key: deployment.region, value: eu-west-1, action: insert }   # only if missing
transform/truncate:              # OTTL: the OpenTelemetry Transformation Language
(regex into new keys). `transform` can do almost anything with OTTL statements and `where` conditions; `filter` drops whatever
its conditions match. Redaction in the Collector protects you **today**, for every service; still fix the source.

steps.title: Apply attribute actions
prompt: Implement the `attributes` processor's actions on one span's attributes.
`record AttrAction(string Key, string Action, string? Value = null);` with `Action` one of `insert`, `update`, `upsert`, `delete`, `hash`.
Write `Dictionary<string, string> Apply(Dictionary<string, string> attrs, List<AttrAction> actions)`: a **new** dictionary, actions
- `insert`: set `Value` only if the key is missing; `update`: only if present; `upsert`: always;
- `delete`: remove the key; `hash`: replace a present value with its SHA-256 as lower-case hex
starter: Dictionary<string, string> Apply(Dictionary<string, string> attrs, List<AttrAction> actions)
solution: Dictionary<string, string> Apply(Dictionary<string, string> attrs, List<AttrAction> actions)
var has = result.TryGetValue(a.Key, out var current);
case "update" when has: result[a.Key] = a.Value!; break;
hints: Check `TryGetValue` before each action: insert, update and hash depend on whether the key is there.
A `switch` with `case "insert" when !has:` guards reads nicely.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoIn = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["user.email"] = "ana@example.com", ["http.request.header.authorization"] = "Bearer x", ["app.plan"] = "pro" };
var dojoOut = Apply(dojoIn, [new("user.email", "hash"), new("http.request.header.authorization", "delete"),
new("deployment.region", "insert", "eu-west-1"), new("app.plan", "insert", "free")]);
Dojo.Eq("email hashed (SHA-256, lower hex)", "e8ed2b5eda0fc9cbbea0a5c3a9e4f8bd40b7b6c1c3c8f8a0b1c7e3d7a5a0d6f3".Length, dojoOut.GetValueOrDefault("user.email")?.Length ?? 0);
Dojo.Eq("the hash is the real SHA-256", Convert.ToHexStringLower(System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256.HashData(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("ana@example.com"))), dojoOut.GetValueOrDefault("user.email"));
Dojo.Check("authorization deleted", !dojoOut.ContainsKey("http.request.header.authorization"), "");
Dojo.Eq("insert adds a missing key", "eu-west-1", dojoOut.GetValueOrDefault("deployment.region"));
Dojo.Eq("insert keeps an existing value", "pro", dojoOut.GetValueOrDefault("app.plan"));
Dojo.Eq("the input is untouched", "ana@example.com", dojoIn["user.email"]);
var dojoUp = Apply(new() { ["a"] = "1" }, [new("a", "update", "2"), new("b", "update", "9"), new("c", "upsert", "3"), new("zz", "hash")]);
Dojo.Eq("update only changes present keys, upsert always sets, hash skips missing", "a=2,c=3", string.Join(",", dojoUp.OrderBy(kv => kv.Key).Select(kv => $"{kv.Key}={kv.Value}")));
record AttrAction(string Key, string Action, string? Value = null);

steps.title: Tail sampling policies
body: decision_wait: 10s                 # wait this long after a trace's first span before deciding
num_traces: 50000                  # traces held in memory while waiting
policies:                          # a trace is kept when ANY policy says sample
- { name: errors, type: status_code, status_code: { status_codes: [ERROR] } }
- { name: slow, type: latency, latency: { threshold_ms: 1000 } }
- { name: vip, type: string_attribute, string_attribute: { key: app.plan, values: [enterprise] } }
- { name: rest, type: probabilistic, probabilistic: { sampling_percentage: 5 } }
Latency is the trace's end-to-end time (latest end minus earliest start). Spans that arrive after the decision are judged by the
decision already made (kept traces keep late spans). Memory is roughly spans per second × `decision_wait` × span size: at 20 000
spans/s and 10 s that is 200 000 spans held at once. And every span of a trace must reach the **same** Collector instance (next lesson).

steps.title: Decide like tail_sampling
prompt: Spans of one complete trace: `record Span(string TraceId, double Start, double End, string Status, Dictionary<string, string> Attrs);`
(milliseconds; `Status` is `ERROR`, `OK` or `UNSET`). Policies: `record Policy(string Type, double Number = 0, string? Key = null, string[]? Values = null);`
Write `string Decide(List<Span> trace, List<Policy> policies)` returning the **name of the first policy type that samples**, or `"drop"`:
- `string_attribute`: some span has attribute `Key` with a value in `Values`;
- `probabilistic`: the trace id's first 16 hex digits as an unsigned number, divided by 2^64, times 100, is below `Number` (a percentage).
solution: "string_attribute" => trace.Any(s => p.Key is not null && s.Attrs.TryGetValue(p.Key, out var v) && (p.Values ?? []).Contains(v)),
hints: A `switch` expression on `p.Type`, one line per policy; return the type of the first one that is true.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoPolicies = new List<Policy> { new("status_code"), new("latency", 1000), new("string_attribute", Key: "app.plan", Values: ["enterprise"]), new("probabilistic", 5) };
Span S(string id, double a, double b, string st = "UNSET", string plan = "free") => new(id, a, b, st, new() { ["app.plan"] = plan });
Dojo.Eq("an error is kept", "status_code", Decide([S("ffff000000000000ffff000000000000", 0, 30), S("ffff000000000000ffff000000000000", 5, 20, "ERROR")], dojoPolicies));
Dojo.Eq("end to end, not per span: 1.2 s", "latency", Decide([S("ffff000000000000ffff000000000000", 0, 400), S("ffff000000000000ffff000000000000", 800, 1200)], dojoPolicies));
Dojo.Eq("an enterprise customer", "string_attribute", Decide([S("ffff000000000000ffff000000000000", 0, 40, plan: "enterprise")], dojoPolicies));
Dojo.Eq("the lucky 5%", "probabilistic", Decide([S("0100000000000000ffff000000000000", 0, 40)], dojoPolicies));
Dojo.Eq("an ordinary trace is dropped", "drop", Decide([S("ffff000000000000ffff000000000000", 0, 40), S("ffff000000000000ffff000000000000", 10, 900)], dojoPolicies));
Dojo.Eq("policy order decides the label", "latency", Decide([S("ffff000000000000ffff000000000000", 0, 1500, "ERROR")], [new("latency", 1000), new("status_code")]));
record Span(string TraceId, double Start, double End, string Status, Dictionary<string, string> Attrs);
record Policy(string Type, double Number = 0, string? Key = null, string[]? Values = null);
